columns.*_std: ensemble standard deviation (epistemic only; excludes CFD modelling error)
columns.extrapolated: true if the point lies outside the surrogate's training ranges

conventions.reference_length: c_ref = sum of element chords; all lengths in the dataset are divided by c_ref
conventions.reference_area: c_ref x unit span (2D, coefficients are per unit span)
conventions.moment_reference_point: main-element quarter chord (on its chord line)
conventions.axes: x downstream (freestream direction), y up, ground plane at y = 0

sign_conventions.cl: positive up (lift); a downforce wing has cl < 0. Downforce coefficient = -cl
sign_conventions.cm: positive nose-up (standard aerodynamic convention), pitch axis -z
sign_conventions.aoa_deg: main-element incidence; positive = leading edge down (more downforce)
sign_conventions.flap_deg: deflection relative to the previous element's chord; positive = TE towards suction side

geometry_definitions.ride_height_over_chord: ground to lowest point of the assembly / c_ref
geometry_definitions.gap_i: min surface distance between element i-1 and element i / c_ref
geometry_definitions.overlap_i: along element i-1 chord, from flap LE to element i-1 TE midpoint / c_ref (+ = flap LE upstream)

use_in_3d: These are 2D sectional coefficients. A lap-time model needs span/area, 3D and endplate corrections, and validation against your STAR-CCM+ or track data.
